title: Hit during personal care
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on an elderly care ward. Mrs Grey, 88, has advanced dementia and was admitted with a urinary tract infection. During personal care, she hits a healthcare assistant, Jo, in the face.

Jo is shaken but not seriously hurt. Mrs Grey is agitated and calling out.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Check that Jo is all right.
options.brief: She has been hurt and may be upset.
options.detailed: Even if not seriously injured, she may be shaken. Checking on her shows support.

options.text: Assess Mrs Grey for pain or delirium.
options.brief: Her behaviour may be a sign of an unmet need.
options.detailed: People with dementia often become agitated because of pain, delirium, or fear. Her infection may be making her more confused. Finding the cause helps.

options.text: Prescribe a sedative to calm her down.
options.brief: Sedation should be a last resort.
options.detailed: Sedatives can worsen delirium and cause falls. Looking for the cause comes first.

options.text: Tell Jo that aggression is part of the job.
options.detailed: Staff do face aggression, but this minimises what happened.

options.text: Record the incident, and review how her care is given.
options.brief: A plan can make care safer for her and staff.
options.detailed: Recording the incident, and reviewing her care, for example with a calm approach or two staff, protects both her and staff.

options.brief: Not appropriate for a patient with dementia and delirium.
options.detailed: Her behaviour is likely caused by her illness, not intent.

options.text: Ask Mrs Grey's family to do her personal care instead.
options.detailed: Family may help calm her, but personal care is the ward's responsibility.

options.text: Ask staff to avoid personal care until she calms down.
options.detailed: A short pause may help, but care can't be avoided indefinitely.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to aggression from a patient with dementia: supporting staff and looking for the cause.
explanation.keyDetails: She has dementia and a UTI. She is agitated. A colleague was hit.
explanation.reasoning: [A] supports Jo, [B] looks for a cause, and [E] makes care safer. The distractors sedate first ([C]), dismiss Jo ([D]), overreact ([F]), or avoid the problem ([G], [H]).
explanation.competing: [C] is the tempting option, but sedation can worsen delirium and should be a last resort.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, caring for patients with dementia; Domain 3, supporting colleagues.
